module.title: JavaScript Fundamentals
module.description: Learn how websites become interactive and dynamic using JavaScript.
learningObjectives: Understand how websites react to users

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: JavaScript is a programming language used to make websites interactive and dynamic.

sections.heading: What Does JavaScript Do?
sections.content: JavaScript adds functionality to websites like buttons, animations, forms, dark mode, sliders, and dynamic updates.

sections.heading: HTML, CSS, And JavaScript Together
sections.content: HTML creates structure, CSS creates design, and JavaScript adds interaction and logic.

sections.heading: Why Websites Need JavaScript
sections.content: Without JavaScript, websites would only display static content and could not react to user actions.

sections.heading: JavaScript Runs In Browser
sections.content: Browsers can directly run JavaScript code to update webpages instantly.

easyExample.title: Robot Example
easyExample.content: If HTML is the body and CSS is the appearance, JavaScript is the brain controlling actions and behavior.

terms.meaning: User actions like clicking or typing

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Variables are containers used to store information in JavaScript.

sections.heading: Why Variables Exist
sections.content: Variables help store and reuse data inside programs.

sections.heading: What Can Variables Store?
sections.content: Variables can store names, numbers, text, passwords, lists, and many other types of information.

sections.heading: Why Data Matters
sections.content: Websites use data constantly for login systems, forms, user profiles, and applications.

sections.heading: Updating Variables
sections.content: Variable values can change while the program is running.

easyExample.title: Box Example
easyExample.content: Think of variables like labeled boxes where you store different items.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks.

sections.heading: Why Functions Exist
sections.content: Functions help organize code and avoid repeating the same logic multiple times.

sections.heading: Reusable Logic
sections.content: Once a function is created, it can be used again whenever needed.

sections.heading: Functions In Real Websites
sections.content: Buttons, form validation, login systems, and API requests all use functions.

sections.heading: Functions Improve Organization
sections.content: Functions make large applications cleaner and easier to manage.

easyExample.title: Coffee Machine Example
easyExample.content: Pressing a coffee machine button performs multiple steps automatically. Functions work similarly.

lessons.title: Conditions And Decisions

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Conditions help programs make decisions based on situations.

sections.heading: Why Conditions Exist
sections.content: Programs need decision-making logic to behave differently in different situations.

sections.heading: Real Website Usage
sections.content: Login systems, authentication, forms, and dashboards all use conditions.

sections.heading: True And False
sections.content: Conditions check whether something is true or false.

sections.heading: Program Flow
sections.content: Conditions decide which code should run.

easyExample.title: Traffic Signal Example
easyExample.content: If the traffic light is green, cars move. Otherwise they stop. Websites use similar decision logic.

terms.meaning: Runs code when condition is true

basicCode.title: Condition Example

summary: Programs react differently based on conditions
if and else control program flow

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Loops repeat code multiple times automatically.

sections.heading: Why Loops Exist
sections.content: Loops prevent developers from writing repetitive code manually.

sections.heading: Repeating Tasks
sections.content: Applications often need to repeat actions like displaying lists or processing data.

sections.heading: Loops Save Time
sections.content: Loops make programs shorter and more efficient.

sections.heading: Where Loops Are Used
sections.content: Loops are used in product lists, user feeds, dashboards, and many other features.

easyExample.title: Attendance Example
easyExample.content: Calling student names one by one manually is repetitive. A loop automates repetitive work.

terms.meaning: Repeats code fixed number of times

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Events allow websites to react to user actions like clicks and typing.

sections.heading: What Is An Event?
sections.content: An event is an action performed by the user such as clicking, typing, scrolling, or hovering.

sections.heading: Why Events Matter
sections.content: Without events, websites could not respond to user actions.

sections.heading: Interactive Websites
sections.content: Buttons, forms, dropdowns, dark mode, and games all rely on events.

sections.heading: Event Listeners
sections.content: Event listeners wait for user actions and run code when events happen.

easyExample.title: Doorbell Example
easyExample.content: A doorbell waits until someone presses it. Event listeners work similarly by waiting for user actions.
